theater: 猶太山地莫德因與耶路撒冷

battle.name: 馬加比起義
battle.theater: 猶太山地莫德因與耶路撒冷
battle.brief: 塞琉古王安提奧庫斯四世禁猶太人守律並掠奪耶路撒冷聖殿，祭司馬他提亞於莫德因起兵，率猶大·馬加比等五子在猶太山地游擊；公元前一百六十四年冬攻入聖殿、重開祭禮，開啟哈斯蒙尼王朝。卡面的科林斯青銅盔代表塞琉古方希臘重裝步兵的典型防具。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 交戰的一方是塞琉古王國。一七五年，塞琉古四世在安提阿被托勒密六世派人毒殺，其弟安提奧庫斯四世與菲利普自巴比倫返國爭位，菲利普旋即病死，安提奧庫斯獨佔王位並把都城安提阿經營成希臘化世界的樞紐。他自稱伊庇法涅斯，在希臘化諸王眼中重整王室權威，在猶太人眼中卻以強制同化與財政榨取施壓。王家軍隊以馬其頓式方陣為骨架，由安提阿與各行省的駐軍、希臘化傭兵、弓箭手與象兵、戰車隊組成；耶路撒冷城內的「阿克拉」要塞則由塞琉古守軍長期駐紮，控制聖殿周邊並監視城門出入，鎮守者多為本地腓尼基與希臘後裔的混編守備。交戰的另一方是猶太聖殿社群與鄉村起義者：耶路撒冷、耶利哥及以色列地各城的祭司、利未人、文士與農戶，編為《馬加比一書》所說的「四個支隊」，以莫德因為據，轉入猶太山地與西側丘陵游擊；其中不少人在塞琉古與外邦軍隊中當過傭兵，熟悉希臘武器、隊形與行軍節奏。起義者後來得到以東人與阿拉伯騎兵的協助，也得到部分被安提奧庫斯冷落的外邦城市同情，形成一個對抗王室的鬆散聯盟。
countriesEn: One side was the Seleucid Empire. In 175 BC Seleucus IV was murdered at Antioch by agents of Ptolemy VI; his brothers Antiochus IV and Philip returned from Babylon to contest the throne, Philip died soon after, and Antiochus ended up as sole ruler, turning Antioch into the hub of the Hellenistic world. He styled himself Epiphanes, the manifest god, and to the other Hellenistic kings he looked like a restorer of royal authority, while to the Judeans he appeared as a face of religious assimilation and financial extraction. The royal army was built around the Macedonian phalanx and consisted of garrison troops from Antioch and the satrapies, Greek mercenaries, archers, war elephants and chariot units; inside Jerusalem, the Seleucid garrison in the citadel known as the Acra held the sanctuary district under watch and controlled the gates, its soldiers a mixed levy of local Phoenician and Greek descent. The other side was the Judean temple community and the rural insurgents: priests, Levites, scribes and farmers from Jerusalem, Jericho and the towns of the countryside, organised into the four squadrons named in the First Book of Maccabees. They took Modin as their base and moved into the Judean hills and the western Shephelah to fight a war of movement. Many of them had served as mercenaries in Seleucid and foreign armies and knew Greek weapons, formations and marching pace well. The insurgents later drew support from Idumean and Arab cavalry and gained sympathy from some foreign cities that Antiochus had alienated, so that a loose coalition against the crown grew up around them.
people: 核心人物是耶路撒冷祭司馬他提亞。他出自後來被稱為哈西德人的虔誠派，長期在莫德因主持禮儀；安提奧庫斯的敕令一到，他當眾殺死在祭壇前違律行祭的官員，又襲擊執行命令的軍官，起義由此點燃。他有五個兒子：猶大·馬加比、約拿單·阿福斯、以利亞撒、西門·他西與約翰，全部加入義軍；父親在一六七年的冬季病逝後，起義由猶大接掌，號稱統帥。猶大是全場最出色的野戰指揮官：他以以瑪谷之戰奠基，率眾攻入耶路撒冷，後來在以瑪谷周邊、伯匝加利與約旦河一線擊潰立西亞與戈爾基阿斯的援軍，最終在西腓一帶戰死。約拿單接任後轉向外交與游擊並用，先後以巴比倫與美索不達米亞的借款支撐軍費，並一度以副手身分主持大祭司職務，後來自立；同時他四出征伐以東，在加里米斯與厄革倫一線取勝，並利用塞琉古將領之間的矛盾削弱敵方。一五七年他迎回兄長西門接任大祭司。西門築「大衛城」並把它與聖殿連成一體，使哈斯蒙尼王朝同時握有宗教與世俗權力，一四三年遭安提拍特派人刺殺；其子約翰·海卡努斯繼位，於一三三年攻毀耶路撒冷城內的阿克拉要塞。塞琉古方面的主角是安提奧庫斯四世本人，其弟菲利普在爭位中病死；將領中以立西亞、戈爾基阿斯、尼卡托與阿布布之子托勒密最為關鍵，各自率軍鎮守或遠征。約瑟夫斯《古史》記安提奧庫斯一六四年在波斯病逝，其子德米特里一世返國即位，隨即不得不與起義者交涉。
peopleEn: The central figure was the Jerusalem priest Mattathias. He came from the pious group later called Hasideans and kept the round of sacrifices at Modin; when the royal order reached the town he killed on the spot the official who offered an illegal sacrifice at the altar, then struck down the officer enforcing the decree, and the revolt began there. He had five sons, Judas Maccabeus, Jonathan Apphus, Eleazar, Simon Thassi and John, and all of them joined him. After the father fell ill and died in the winter of 167 BC the command passed to Judas, who was given the title of commander. Judas proved the finest field general of the revolt: he founded his reputation at Emmaus, entered Jerusalem with his brothers, and then broke Lysias and Gorgias in the fighting around Emmaus, Beth Zechariah and the approaches to the Jordan, before he was killed in Idumea. Jonathan took over and mixed war with negotiation, borrowing money from Babylon and Mesopotamia to pay his men, and serving for a time as deputy in the high priestly office before he took it himself; at the same time he campaigned in Idumea, won in the region of Garizim and Ekron, and used the quarrels between rival Seleucid generals to weaken the enemy. In 157 BC he brought his brother Simon back to succeed him. Simon walled the citadel of David and joined it to the temple, so that the Hasmonean house held religious and civil power at once, and he was assassinated by men of Antipater in 143 BC; his son John Hyrcanus succeeded him and destroyed the Seleucid Acra in Jerusalem in 133 BC. The leading figure on the Seleucid side was Antiochus IV himself, whose brother Philip died during the struggle for the crown; among the generals Lysias, Gorgias, Nicator and Ptolemy son of Abubus mattered most, each holding a province or leading a field army. Josephus records that Antiochus died in Persia in 164 BC, that his son Demetrius I returned to rule, and that he soon found himself having to negotiate with the insurgents.
kits: 卡面這頂科林斯青銅盔，是希臘重裝步兵最典型的頭部防具：全銅或銅錫合金的殼體，兩側可轉的護頰把臉罩住，鼻梁垂下成護鼻，後緣有護頸，盔頂有羽冠插座。要提醒的是，公元前二世紀的希臘化軍隊普遍改用較輕便的阿提卡式盔，只留短護頰與頂盔飾，所以科林斯盔在安提奧庫斯四世時代已屬舊式，但它仍是「希臘全套武裝」最完整的標誌：塞琉古方陣以薩里沙長矛（六米以上）、大型凸面圓盾、亞麻布或鑲片胸甲、青銅脛甲組成，卡面上這頂盔正是方陣前排的標準配備，而盔上開眼的設計意味著戴盔者只能靠隊形而非視野自保。反觀起義者，義軍主力是輕裝步兵與神射手，靠長矛、投槍、弓箭與擲石索作戰，靠速度和地形取勝，並非列陣而進；文獻記載他們「像戰士一樣束上甲胄」，使用希臘式長矛與盾牌，但全軍只有部分人著甲。攻城方面，義軍以圍城、封鎖路口與突擊對付耶路撒冷阿克拉要塞、厄革倫與伯夆等據點，塞琉古方面則配備象隊、戰車與各類攻城器械。補給靠鄉村糧秣與城鎮徵集，趕路多靠步行、騾馬與有限車輛；武器來源一部分是外邦傭兵裝備與散落的王軍器械，一部分來自城內作坊的銅鐵鍛打。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on this card is the classic headgear of the Greek heavy infantry: a shell of bronze or copper alloy, hinged cheek pieces that close over the face, a nasal guard hanging down over the nose, a neck guard at the rear, and a socket in the crown for a horsehair crest. One caveat is worth stating: in the second century BC Hellenistic armies had generally moved to the lighter Attic helmet with short cheek pieces and a decorated crown, so by the time of Antiochus IV the Corinthian form was already old. It nevertheless remains the clearest sign of the full Greek panoply, and that is exactly what the Seleucid phalanx fielded: long sarissa pikes over six metres, large convex round shields, linen or plated body armour, and bronze greaves. The helmet on the card belonged to a soldier in the front rank of such a formation, and its narrow field of vision shows that such a man could only survive through the wall of shields in front of him. The insurgents were the opposite. Their strength was light infantry and missile troops using javelins, bows, slings and stones, winning by speed and knowledge of the ground rather than by marching in line; the sources say they girded themselves like warriors and used Greek style spears and shields, but only part of the force was armoured at all. On the siege side the rebels relied on blockade, the closing of passes and sudden assault against the Acra in Jerusalem, the fortress at Ekron and Beth Zur, while the Seleucids brought elephants, chariots and a full range of siege engines. Logistics ran on grain and wine levied from the villages, on foot, mule and horse, and on a small number of carts. Arms came partly from foreign mercenary kit and from the scattered equipment of royal columns, partly from the copper and iron workshops of the towns.
tactics: 起義的第一手是地形。義軍據莫德因，這座小城距耶路撒冷約三十公里，扼住通往沿海的丘陵道路；一六七年的冬季，馬他提亞在莫德因同時打擊違律者與王軍守官，義軍隨即以縱隊分散躲入猶太山地，遊走於耶路撒冷西北的丘陵與谷地之間。第二次戰役以瑪谷是典型：塞琉古軍在以瑪谷集結，猶大從高地俯衝，摧毀其營地，殺傷約八百人、擊潰約三千人，切斷通往耶路撒冷的補給線；緊接的卡帕沙拉瑪之戰採夜襲，義軍分隊同時點火衝營，把方陣營地打成混戰。卡帕沙拉瑪與伯霍隆兩役顯示，義軍靠小分隊、夜間行動與攻擊敵營弱點取勝，並在勝利後立刻收繳器械與旗幟，再退回山中。塞琉古方則以馬其頓方陣正面進攻，長矛密集、結陣徐進，試圖以厚度壓制義軍；聖殿陷落後，王軍退守城內要塞。之後雙方進入長期消耗：義軍以圍城、切斷糧道、奪取隘口為主，國王遠征時利用其缺席反擊，約拿單甚至利用敵方將領間的矛盾分化敵營。一六一年的約旦河畔，義軍一度潰散，退入曠野地帶的塔，翌年再整軍出擊；一六〇年猶大在西腓一帶的戰役失利陣亡，分隊隨即解體。整體看，雙方在武器上是不對稱的：一方是配備完整而訓練有素的重裝方陣，一方是裝備簡陋但機動性高、熟悉地形的游擊隊伍。
tacticsEn: The first move of the revolt was terrain. Modin, a small town about thirty kilometres from Jerusalem, commands the hill roads that lead towards the coastal plain. In the winter of 167 BC Mattathias struck the transgressor and the royal officer at the same moment at Modin, and the insurgents immediately scattered into the Judean hills in separate columns, moving between the valleys and ridges north-west of Jerusalem. The second action, at Emmaus, shows their method. The royal force was assembled in the plain at Emmaus; Judas fell on it from the higher ground, broke up the camp, killed about eight hundred men and routed some three thousand, and cut the supply road to Jerusalem. The night attack at Capaar-salama followed, the insurgents striking several camps at once with torches so that the phalanx formations dissolved into confusion. Capaar-salama and Beth-horon together show how small mobile bands worked by night movement and by attacking the weak parts of a camp, and then seized weapons, standards and booty before withdrawing into the hills. The Seleucids replied in the classical way, advancing in a dense Macedonian phalanx with levelled pikes and trying to crush the insurgents by sheer weight. After the fall of the sanctuary the royal troops fell back into the citadel inside the city. The war then settled into a long attritional contest in which the rebels used blockade, the cutting of supplies and control of the mountain passes, and attacked whenever the king was away on campaign; Jonathan even exploited the quarrels between rival royal generals. At the Jordan in 161 BC the insurgent army was broken and driven into the desert, where it reformed and came back the next year. In 160 BC Judas was defeated and killed in the Idumean campaign, and the columns dissolved. The whole conflict was a fight between unequalled weapons: on one side a fully equipped and well drilled phalanx, on the other a lightly armed irregular force whose advantage was mobility and local knowledge of the ground.
data: 可核對的數字多來自《馬加比一書》的敘述。年份方面：一七五年塞琉古四世被殺、一六七年的「第一百四十五年」起義（該書三章一節）、一六四年十二月二十五日聖殿重新奉獻，均為傳統紀年的基準。日曆上，敕令與褻瀆聖殿記在基斯流月十五日，聖殿重修慶典則自基斯流月二十五日起，慶祝八日。兵力方面：塞琉古方面的分遣隊，史料記有步兵一萬一千與騎兵一千，以及步兵二萬、騎兵五千、戰車三千的混合大軍；十一章五節記立西亞的援軍為步兵二萬、騎兵五千，作戰中亦見象隊。義軍方面沒有可靠總數，僅可見各戰役的局部數字：以瑪谷之戰義軍殺傷約八百、擊潰約三千；卡帕沙拉瑪之戰追擊殲滅敵軍步兵五千與騎兵八百；伯霍隆一役義軍斬獲逾五千；九章記義軍面對的敵軍兵力被描述為三十萬之眾，該數字當屬文學性誇大。器械與財貨方面，二書五章記聖殿被掠時所奪銀錢達二千他拉得；他拉得為金衡單位。距離則在數十公里量級：莫德因在耶路撒冷西北約三十公里，以瑪谷在西約三十公里，伯夆在南方約二十公里，這些距離決定了義軍夜間行軍與襲擾的可行性。
dataEn: The verifiable figures come chiefly from the narrative of the First Book of Maccabees. On chronology: 175 BC for the murder of Seleucus IV, the hundred and forty-fifth year, that is 167 BC, for the rising (3:1), and the twenty-fifth of Kislev 164 BC for the re-dedication of the temple are the standard points of reference. The calendar matters: the decree and the profanation of the sanctuary are dated to the fifteenth of Kislev, while the festival of the re-dedication began on the twenty-fifth of Kislev and lasted eight days. On troops, the sources give the royal detachments as eleven thousand foot and a thousand horse, and as a mixed column of twenty thousand foot, five thousand horse and three thousand chariots; 11:5 gives Lysias a relief force of twenty thousand foot and five thousand horse, and elephants were in use as well. The insurgents have no reliable total, only local figures from single actions: at Emmaus they killed about eight hundred and routed about three thousand; at Capaar-salama they pursued and destroyed about five thousand foot and eight hundred horse; at Beth-horon they took more than five thousand. The ninth chapter describes the enemy host revealed to Jonathan as three hundred thousand strong, a figure best treated as literary exaggeration. On booty and money, 2 Maccabees 5 gives the silver taken from the temple treasury as about two thousand talents, the talent being a weight of precious metal. Distances are on a scale of tens of kilometres: Modin lies about thirty kilometres north-west of Jerusalem, Emmaus about thirty kilometres to the west, and Beth Zur about twenty kilometres to the south, and those figures decide whether a night march and a surprise attack were possible at all.
cause: 起義的直接原因是塞琉古王室的宗教打壓與制度掠奪。安提奧庫斯四世既要為對抗托勒密王朝的戰爭籌措軍資，也要在希臘化諸城推行對宙斯的崇拜。他拆毀耶路撒冷舊有的城門祭壇，於聖殿內設立宙斯的祭壇，沒收聖殿器皿作為抵押，派遣官員監督城內各處，強迫居民改信，並下令廢除《利未記》所定的一切律法，禁守逾太節與安息日。老祭司歐尼亞斯三世的孫子安尼亞斯四世被免職，由一個本無祭司血統、靠行賄取得爵位的梅涅勞斯出任大祭司，此舉同時激起祭司階層與民間的反感；城中部分猶太上層家庭改信並購得官職，塞琉古的硬性措施隨即延伸到教育層面：講授律法的文士被處死，律法書被焚毀，城郊的莊園與武庫被攻破。安提奧庫斯還在安提阿鑄造帶宙斯雙騎像與亞歷山大盾形符號的新幣，流通到聖殿地區，等於以貨幣承認新神新話。此外，安提阿的居民議會也發出要求全境城市效忠的文書，塞琉古的統治因此被一部分外邦人視為暴政，這種外交孤立使安提奧庫斯在猶太地區推行命令時缺少其他勢力的掩護。
causeEn: The immediate cause was religious repression and institutional dispossession on the part of the Seleucid crown. Antiochus IV needed money for the war against the Ptolemies and wanted the cult of Zeus enforced in the Hellenistic cities. He pulled down the old altar of burnt offering at the gate of Jerusalem, set up an altar to Zeus inside the sanctuary, took the vessels of the temple as security against a loan, posted officers to supervise the city, and forbade everything the Law of Leviticus prescribed, including the keeping of the pilgrim festivals and the Sabbath. The legitimate line of Onias III was set aside: his grandson Onias IV was removed from office and Menelaus, a man without priestly descent who had bought the post with money, was installed as high priest, which enraged both the priestly order and the people. Some of the wealthier Judean families conformed, took posts and even bought ranks, and the pressure was then extended to education: teachers of the Law were put to death, law books were burned, and estates and armoury outside the city were broken into. Antiochus also struck new coinage at Antioch carrying the mounted Dioscuri and the Macedonian shield, and that money circulated in the sanctuary district, so even the currency recognised the new gods. The Athenians, and other Hellenistic communities that Antiochus had offended, sent letters and decrees pressing the cities to remain loyal, and the king was therefore isolated abroad; that isolation left him with few partners when he enforced his orders in Judea.
impact: 這場起義改變了猶太地區的權力結構。原本依附王室的大祭司職位在混亂中失去正當性：起義者以「撒都西人一族」自居，最後連大祭司的任命權也由掌握武力的政治集團接管，《馬加比一書》第九卷因約拿單任職而中斷，被後世視為經卷記錄告一段落的標記。宗教層面上，聖殿在敗亂後重新奉獻，基斯流月二十五日被固定為八日的紀念節日，形成此後猶太曆法中與聖殿相關的重要節期；文獻中的「奧德賽」式頌詩（如《馬加比二書》第二章）被拿來解釋為何一小隊人足以擊敗大軍。政治層面上，義軍清除了聖殿區的塞琉古據點與異教設施，耶路撒冷因此在數十年內維持相對的自治，同時哈斯蒙尼王朝在希臘化諸王之間周旋求生。思想層面，後來死海古卷「戰爭卷」中的「北方之星」與「祭司君王」形象，以及「四個支隊」編制的希臘式痕跡，都常被學者拿來與馬加比時代的經驗對照。更長遠看，這場戰爭把耶路撒冷變成一個以武器與祭司為核心的政治中心，其後的哈斯蒙尼王朝正是由此起步；約翰·海卡努斯與哈西德派的決裂以及伊都瑪利人安提拍特的崛起，又把羅馬的干預逐步帶進這片地區。
impactEn: The revolt reorganised power in Judea. The office of high priest, which had depended on the royal house, lost its legitimacy in the confusion and was taken over by a political faction: the insurgents presented themselves as the Hasidean party, and eventually even the appointment of the high priest passed to the men who held armed strength. The First Book of Maccabees breaks off in its ninth chapter at the point where Jonathan takes office, and later readers took that break as the mark of the end of the written record. At the religious level the sanctuary was re-dedicated after its desecration, and the twenty-fifth of Kislev was fixed as an eight day festival, which remains a calendrical marker tied to the temple. The poetic and figurative literature of the period, such as the Odyssey style passage in 2 Maccabees 2, was used to explain how a small band could defeat a great army. Politically the insurgents cleared the Seleucid strongpoints and the pagan installations out of the sanctuary area, so that Jerusalem enjoyed a long period of relative autonomy, while the Hasmonean dynasty manoeuvred for survival between the rival Hellenistic kings. In the longer term the war turned Jerusalem into a political centre built on arms and priesthood, and the Hasmonean house grew out of it; the later quarrel of John Hyrcanus with the Hasideans and the rise of the Idumean Antipater brought Roman intervention steadily closer to this region.
result: 馬加比起義的直接結果，是塞琉古對耶路撒冷聖殿的實際控制被打破。猶大在聖殿重新奉獻之後仍南征北戰，一六〇年在西腓一帶戰死，義軍一度瓦解，兄長約拿單重整旗鼓，在安提奧庫斯四世死後的權力真空中以交涉換取合法性：猶太議會在高門內正式立約拿單為大祭司，他隨後又取得世俗的省長頭銜，並靠外邦借款維持軍隊。他西征以東，在加里米斯與厄革倫一帶取勝，一五七年迎回其兄西門接任大祭司。西門把「大衛城」與聖殿連成一體並加以固守，確立了哈斯蒙尼王朝同時握有教權與政權的格局；一五三年他遣使往安提阿，最終取得大祭司與省長的合併確認，因此被以東人安提拍特視為障礙，一四三年安提拍特派人暗殺西門。其子約翰·海卡努斯接位後逐步削弱安提拍特的勢力，一三三年攻毀耶路撒冷城內的塞琉古阿克拉要塞，至此耶路撒冷完全脫離塞琉古守軍的控制。這場戰爭沒有帶來耶路撒冷國家的完全獨立，塞琉古王國在此後仍捲入與帕提亞人的長期戰爭，但宗教禁令被廢除、聖殿重建、祭司制度改組與哈斯蒙尼王朝的建立，都是不可逆的結果。
resultEn: The immediate result of the Maccabean revolt was the end of effective Seleucid control over the Jerusalem sanctuary. Judas carried the war on after the re-dedication and was killed in Idumea in 160 BC, the insurgent columns dissolved, and the surviving brothers rebuilt the movement. In the political vacuum left by the death of Antiochus IV, Jonathan traded armed action for recognition: the Jewish assembly in the great hall formally installed him as high priest, he later took the secular title of governor, and he paid his troops with money borrowed from foreign courts. He campaigned in Idumea, won in the region of Garizim and Ekron, and in 157 BC brought his brother Simon back to succeed him. Simon united the citadel of David with the temple area and fortified it, and established the Hasmonean pattern in which Simon and his successors held both the priesthood and the civil authority. In 153 BC he sent an embassy to Antioch and obtained the recognition of the combined office of priest and governor, which made him the object of the Idumean Antipater's hatred, and Antipater had him assassinated in 143 BC. His son John Hyrcanus took over, steadily cut down Antipater's position and destroyed the Seleucid Acra in Jerusalem in 133 BC, and from that point Jerusalem was free of the Seleucid garrison. The war did not create a fully independent Judean state, and the Seleucid kingdom remained entangled for decades in its long wars with Parthia, but the repeal of the religious decrees, the re-dedication of the temple, the reorganisation of the priesthood and the foundation of the Hasmonean dynasty were all irreversible.
